newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch shares close 1.24 pct lower after U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: Dutch shares close 1.24 pct lower after U.S. data.

text.p: Dutch shares closed 1.24 percent lower on Friday, depressed by a big fall on Wall Street after U.S. producer prices data for March raised fresh concerns about U.S. inflation and another interest rate hike.
U.S. producer prices fell 0.1 percent in March but the core component, stripping out food and energy components, rose 0.4 percent -- much higher than had been expected.

The AEX index which been idling in positive territory before the 1230 GMT release of the U.S. data, dropped on the news and then fell further to close 9.09 points lower at 724.38 as Wall Street lost almost 80 points in the early part of its session.
"The PPI figure was disappointing. The impact was felt in the bonds and that spread out quickly into the share market," said one dealer.

"Basically the figures could mean higher interest rates in the U.S., but it's difficult to say when because the next FOMC meeting isn't until May," he added. The Federal Reserve's policy making Open Market Committee is scheduled to meet on May 23.

Other dealers said trading volumes had been thin throughout the day as investors settled down to wait for the U.S. data. "We've had such low turnover today that it was pretty easy to put downward pressure on the market," said one.

Analysts said the surprise jump in the core rate coupled with stronger U.S. first quarter retail sales also put pressure on prices. March retail sales rose 0.2 percent, lower than expected, but January and February figures were revised upwards.
Wall Street was down around 70 points by the time the Amsterdam market closed but dealers said sentiment in the U.S. could prove difficult to read in the wake of the data.

"Wall Street could be down 100 points when we come in on Monday and that will have an obvious impact on us," said a dealer. He added, however, that the fall in Amsterdam had reflected absence of buyers rather than sustained selling.
